levels.name: Mia, 19, Student
levels.story: The 8 levels of rent prices. Level 1. 450 Dollar Miete, und mein Vermieter will mich auf den Müll werfen, während ich für mein Krankenpflege-Studium blute. Level one. $450 rent a month – and my landlord is throwing me into the garbage by Friday while I bleed for my nursing degree. I am Mia, 19, working at an exhausting diner while studying nursing, staring at my glowing red forehead badge in the cracked bathroom mirror. My tiny closet room smells of damp cardboard, mold, and cheap instant noodles, while my bank account shows an empty balance of exactly forty-two dollars. Then my phone buzzes aggressively on the mattress, shattering the silence. A text from my landlord pops up with a cold ultimatum, mocking my desperate situation. I grab my worn backpack and rush down the hallway, clutching my last twenty-dollar bill with trembling fingers. Pay your full deposit today or get out, you broke student. What was written inside the eviction notice stamped with a red urgent seal? Das siehst du in Level 2. You'll see that in Level 2.

levels.name: Leo, 24, Barista
levels.story: The 8 levels of rent prices. Level 2. 850 Dollar Miete für eine mickrige Garage, und mein eiskalter Vermieter reißt dem armen Barista vor meinen Augen die geliebte Kaffeemaschine weg, bevor er die Miete verdoppelt. Level two. $850 rent for a converted garage – and my ice-cold landlord rips the beloved coffee machine away from the poor barista right before my eyes and doubles the rent without warning. I am Leo, 24, pulling espresso shots at dawn while my aching legs burn from twelve-hour shifts at the cafe. A gold coin rests on the counter near my meager tips, and my forehead badge glows a stubborn, harsh yellow indicating my financial trap. A regular customer in a tailored suit drops a massive tip, but it is never enough to cover the soaring cost of living in this unforgiving neighborhood. My landlord stomps into the shop, slams his fist on the counter, and sneers directly in my face. You are two weeks behind on utilities, or your worthless stuff goes on the street tonight. Who slipped the mysterious white envelope under the front door at midnight? Das siehst du in Level 3. You'll see that in Level 3.

levels.name: Sam, 31, Artisan
levels.story: The 8 levels of rent prices. Level 3. 1.400 Dollar Miete für eine dunkle Kellerwerkstatt, während die Stadt die Grundsteuer verdoppelt und Victor mich gnadenlos ausraubt. Level three. $1,400 a month for a basement workshop while the city doubles the property tax and Victor ruthlessly robs me blind. I am Sam, 31, carving custom wooden chairs while thick sawdust clings to my heavy green coat. My forehead badge glows a steady blue, reminding me of my precarious middle-tier standing. Across the narrow alley, I can see the bus stop where Mia waits every single morning, shivering in the cold. My arrogant landlord storms down the concrete steps without knocking, smelling of expensive cologne and cheap cigars, holding a termination notice. If you do not pay the outrageous new commercial surcharge by noon, your tools get impounded forever. What was hidden inside the locked floor safe beneath the old wooden rug? Das siehst du in Level 4. You'll see that in Level 4.

levels.name: Chloe, 28, Designer

levels.name: The Executive, 60, Mastermind
levels.story: The 8 levels of rent prices. Level 8. 15.000 Dollar Miete für das gesamte Kronenanwesen, während Mia mir als gerissene Rebellin das Monopol entreißt. Level eight. $15,000 a month for the entire crown estate while Mia tears my monopoly apart as a fierce rebel. I am the Executive, 60, watching the entire human drama unfold from the highest glass spire in Gotham Greens. My forehead badge glows an endless, blinding platinum of absolute power. Down on the pavement below, I see Mia, Leo, Sam, Chloe, Marcus, Victor, and Julian all crossing paths in the central plaza. They thought the numbers defined their human worth, but the entire housing system was just a ruthless game I designed. The number on your forehead never lies, but it can always be rewritten if you play your cards right. Which topic should we explore in the next series about the hidden numbers of Gotham Greens?
